explanation.headline: Overvalued · 36/100
explanation.body: The composite score is 36/100, in the Overvalued band. Long-term valuation reads 26/100 (Overvalued), while current market conditions read 61/100 (Supportive). The score summarizes historical relative attractiveness across four categories; it is not an objective measure of intrinsic value.

conflicts: Long-term valuation is less attractive than current market conditions. The composite blends a weak valuation signal with more supportive conditions.
data_notes: Market breadth uses the current S&P 500 constituent list across history. The series is survivorship-biased and is not a fully representative point-in-time history.
The Buffett Indicator is displayed as supplementary evidence and carries zero weight in the composite.
CNN Fear & Greed, when available, is transformed directly (100 - index) rather than percentile-ranked.
The equity risk premium is a trailing earnings-yield proxy, not a full expected-return model.
One or more percentiles use a shorter window than the 20-year default because the available history is shorter. The component cards disclose the window actually used.
explanation.disclaimer: This dashboard is a historical relative-attractiveness summary, not a forecast, an intrinsic-value estimate, or an automated buy/sell signal. A low score is not a sell instruction and a high score is not a buy instruction.

indicators.name: Shiller CAPE Ratio
indicators.description: The S&P 500 real price divided by the 10-year average of inflation-adjusted earnings.
indicators.methodology: Published Shiller CAPE: the S&P 500 real price divided by the average of the preceding ten years of inflation-adjusted earnings. The published series is used without re-estimation.
indicators.limitations: Monthly data. The newest month is a preliminary estimate and is excluded from scores until its publication lag has elapsed. The series uses current-vintage history, so historical revisions are not captured. CAPE is a slow-moving valuation measure and says little about near-term returns.

indicators.name: S&P 500 Forward P/E
indicators.description: The S&P 500 price divided by consensus next-twelve-month earnings.
indicators.methodology: S&P 500 price divided by FactSet's bottom-up consensus estimate of earnings for the next twelve months, as stated in FactSet's weekly Earnings Insight report. The value is read from the report text (one decimal place) and stored with the report date as both the observation and release date.
indicators.limitations: Weekly, rounded to one decimal, and parsed from a PDF, so a change in FactSet's wording can pause updates until the parser is fixed. History starts from the first report that was fetched, so percentile scores are weak until a backfill has been run. Check FactSet's terms of use before redistributing the series. Trailing P/E is never substituted and relabeled as forward P/E.
indicators.unavailable_reason: No forward P/E observations have been loaded yet. The refresh workflow reads FactSet's weekly Earnings Insight report into data/forward_pe.csv; run it once with a backfill start date, or set FORWARD_PE_CSV_URL to another authorized date,value CSV.

indicators.name: Buffett Indicator
indicators.description: U.S. listed equity market capitalization as a percentage of nominal GDP.
indicators.source_name: World Bank (market capitalization of listed domestic companies / GDP)
indicators.methodology: Market capitalization of listed domestic companies as a percentage of GDP, as published by the World Bank from World Federation of Exchanges data. The series is shown as supplementary evidence and carries zero weight in the composite.
indicators.limitations: Annual frequency with a substantial publication lag. Coverage is listed domestic companies, not every U.S.-listed issuer, and U.S. companies earn significant revenue abroad. It is supplementary evidence, not a timing tool or a fourth valuation vote.

indicators.name: Equity Risk Premium (proxy)
indicators.description: An earnings-yield-based proxy for the compensation offered by equities over Treasuries.
indicators.methodology: Preferred method: forward earnings yield (1 / forward P/E) minus the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield. When no licensed forward P/E is available, the dashboard uses a clearly labeled trailing proxy: Shiller nominal trailing earnings divided by the S&P 500 price, minus the 10-year Treasury yield. Both legs are nominal.
indicators.limitations: The fallback is an earnings-yield proxy, not a full expected-return model. It ignores growth, payout policy, buybacks, and risk premia embedded in forward estimates. The preferred forward-based version requires licensed forward earnings.

indicators.name: CNN Fear & Greed Index
indicators.description: CNN Business's composite measure of market fear and greed, on a 0-100 scale.
indicators.methodology: CNN Fear & Greed Index on its published 0-100 scale. The component is contrarian: score = 100 - index. Fear can create opportunity but is not proof of undervaluation.
indicators.limitations: No public authorized API is bundled. The indicator stays unavailable unless an authorized feed is configured. A separate VIX/RSI sentiment proxy is displayed and explicitly labeled; it is not substituted for CNN data.
indicators.unavailable_reason: Requires an authorized CNN Fear & Greed feed. Set FEAR_GREED_CSV_URL or import a licensed CSV. An independent daily Fear & Greed index is available from FearGreedChart.com (free API, history from Oct 2016, CORS-enabled). A labeled VIX/RSI proxy is shown in the summary.

indicators.name: Cboe Volatility Index (VIX)
indicators.description: The options-implied expected 30-day volatility of the S&P 500.
indicators.methodology: Cboe VIX closing level. The component is contrarian: higher VIX (more fear) maps to a higher score through an inverse historical percentile.
indicators.limitations: Elevated VIX is not proof that equities are cheap. VIX measures implied volatility and can remain elevated during prolonged drawdowns. It is a supplementary sentiment and risk indicator.

indicators.name: S&P 500 RSI (14-day)
indicators.description: Wilder's 14-day Relative Strength Index of the S&P 500 price index.
indicators.methodology: Wilder's RSI with a 14-period lookback, computed from daily S&P 500 closing prices. The component is contrarian: lower RSI maps to a higher score through an inverse historical percentile. Conventional 30/70 reference levels are displayed.
indicators.limitations: RSI is a price-momentum measure, not a fundamental valuation measure. It can remain oversold or overbought for extended periods. The 30/70 levels are conventions, not statistically validated thresholds.

indicators.name: S&P 500 vs 200-day Moving Average
indicators.description: The percentage distance between the S&P 500 and its 200-trading-day simple moving average.
indicators.methodology: Percentage deviation of the S&P 500 close from its 200-trading-day simple moving average. The component is trend-oriented: higher deviation maps to a higher score through a historical percentile. A zero line marks the moving average.
indicators.limitations: This is primarily a trend indicator, not a valuation measure. A market above its 200-day average can still be expensive, and a market below it can still be cheap.

indicators.name: S&P 500 Constituents Above 200-day Average
indicators.description: The percentage of current S&P 500 constituents trading above their own 200-day averages.
indicators.methodology: For each trading day, the percentage of the current S&P 500 constituent list whose adjusted close exceeds its own 200-trading-day simple moving average. The component is trend-oriented: higher breadth maps to a higher score through a historical percentile.
indicators.limitations: Current constituents are used for the whole history, so the series has survivorship bias and is not a fully representative point-in-time history. History is limited to the configured lookback (six years by default). Adjusted closes are used for splits and distributions. This is a breadth condition, not a valuation measure.

indicators.name: Equal-weight vs Cap-weight S&P 500
indicators.description: Cumulative relative performance of the equal-weighted S&P 500 versus the cap-weighted index.
indicators.source_name: RSP and SPY adjusted closes (total-return proxy)
indicators.methodology: The ratio of RSP (Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF) adjusted close to SPY (SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust) adjusted close. Both series are normalized to 100 at their first common date for cumulative performance. The score uses the historical percentile of the 252-trading-day change in the ratio. Higher values indicate broader participation; the signal is not independently sufficient to establish overvaluation.
indicators.limitations: Adjusted ETF closes approximate total return with distributions reinvested; they are not an official total-return index. RSP inception is 2003. The ratio reflects concentration in large caps but has many other drivers.
